Consider MRO when obtaining marks for classes
When using pytest markers in two baseclasses `Foo` and `Bar`, inheriting from both of those baseclasses will lose the markers of one of those classes. This behavior is present in pytest 3-6, and I think it may as well have been intended. I am still filing it as a bug because I am not sure if this edge case was ever explicitly considered.

If it is widely understood that all markers are part of a single attribute, I guess you could say that this is just expected behavior as per MRO. However, I'd argue that it would be more intuitive to attempt to merge marker values into one, possibly deduplicating marker names by MRO.

```python
import itertools
import pytest

class BaseMeta(type):
    @property
    def pytestmark(self):
        return (
            getattr(self, "_pytestmark", []) +
            list(itertools.chain.from_iterable(getattr(x, "_pytestmark", []) for x in self.__mro__))
        )

    @pytestmark.setter
    def pytestmark(self, value):
        self._pytestmark = value


class Base(object):
    # Without this metaclass, foo and bar markers override each other, and test_dings
    # will only have one marker
    # With the metaclass, test_dings will have both
    __metaclass__ = BaseMeta

@pytest.mark.foo
class Foo(Base):
    pass


@pytest.mark.bar
class Bar(Base):
    pass

class TestDings(Foo, Bar):
    def test_dings(self):
        # This test should have both markers, foo and bar.
        # In practice markers are resolved using MRO (so foo wins), unless the
        # metaclass is applied
        pass
```

I'd expect `foo` and `bar` to be markers for `test_dings`, but this only actually is the case with this metaclass.

Please note that the repro case is Python 2/3 compatible excluding how metaclasses are added to `Base` (this needs to be taken care of to repro this issue on pytest 6)

Now I understand the issue clearly. `get_unpacked_marks(obj)` reads `obj.pytestmark` which uses Python's normal attribute lookup (MRO). When a class `TestDings(Foo, Bar)` has both `Foo` and `Bar` with `pytestmark`, MRO resolution means `TestDings.pytestmark` returns only `Bar`'s (the last one in MRO), losing `Foo`'s marks.

The fix: `get_unpacked_marks` should merge marks from all classes in the MRO, deduplicating by mark name (keeping MRO order). Let me implement this.

# ``Mark`` objects are not hashable (their ``kwargs`` is a mapping), so we
    # deduplicate using a hashable representation of ``(name, args, kwargs)``.
    seen_keys = set()
    unpacked_marks = []

    def _add(mark: Mark) -> None:
        key = (mark.name, mark.args, tuple(sorted(mark.kwargs.items())))
        if key not in seen_keys:
            seen_keys.add(key)
            unpacked_marks.append(mark)

goals.text: Fix missing pytest marks on a class inheriting from two base classes each with a distinct @pytest.mark, so both inherited markers are collected instead of only the first per MRO.
Fix the TypeError introduced by MRO-merging in get_unpacked_marks by making the dedup key hashable (kwargs is an unhashable dict).

facts.text: Bug: a class inheriting from two base classes Foo and Bar, each with a distinct @pytest.mark, loses one marker because pytestmark is resolved via MRO (last wins).
get_unpacked_marks() reads obj.pytestmark via getattr (follows MRO, collapses overlapping base marks) and populates own_markers; Mark is unhashable (kwargs is a dict).
Real pytest collection of TestDings(Foo, Bar) exposed only the foo mark; -m bar selected nothing, confirming the bug.
Existing tests test_mark_decorator_baseclasses_merged and test_mark_decorator_subclass_does_not_propagate_to_base must not be broken by the fix.

changedPaths.text: Proposed to modify get_unpacked_marks() in src/_pytest/mark/structures.py to merge marks across the object's MRO with a hashable dedup key. The edit was applied to the workspace file but never saved to disk.

tests.text: Reproduction collected TestDings::test_dings; with the unsaved MRO-merging edit it then raised TypeError: unhashable type: 'dict' during collection.
Assertion-based reproduction (TestDings(Foo, Bar) with foo/bar marks) failed because TestDings.pytestmark returned only ['foo']; the bar assertion failed.

unfinished.text: No fix was implemented or saved. get_unpacked_marks() still uses the original MRO-collapsing implementation, and the reproduction only confirms the bug.
A real fix and a focused regression test in the pytest suite remain, plus a deduplication key that works for unhashable Mark objects (e.g. sorted kwargs items).

uncertainties.text: Whether merging marks across the MRO in get_unpacked_marks() is the minimal, correct fix, or whether it risks marker duplication/ordering regressions for existing tests.
Whether the intended fix should also change own_markers population in python.py or only get_unpacked_marks().
